In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed security treatment is the best possible one in the sense that it is tight, modular, and captures all known schemes in the random-oracle model.
the security of a blind signature scheme is equivalent to the security of the underlying identification scheme.

our treatment of blind signatures is the first that is able to prove security of the most prominent schemes in the literature, i.e. the Chaum-Camenisch-Stormer, the Chaum-Lindskog, and the Chaum-Pedersen blind signatures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a modular treatment of blind signature security that is based on identification schemes and that is independent of the underlying signature scheme.
we show that the security of a large class of blind signatures derived form identification schemes can be reduced to the security of the corresponding identification scheme.
we provide a general framework for blind signatures from linear identification schemes that captures the security of all schemes from the literature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the One-More-Man-In-The-Middle Security notion is sufficient to prove the security of blind signatures.
we can prove the security of several blind signature schemes in the random-oracle model without having to rely on any additional assumptions.
the classical One-M ore-Unforgeability notion can be seen as a special case of the One-More-Man-In-the-Middle Security notion for identification schemes.
